description: Ledger of operation-id-shaped tokens that canonical artifacts name while operation-registry.json does not list them. An artifact that names an operation id is telling a runner which entry point to exercise; when the id is unregistered the case cannot be run at all, and a deleted wire surface leaves no other trace. check_artifact_operation_id_references consults this ledger. Two kinds are admissible and they are not the same thing: negative_token is a fixture deliberately naming an unregistered token so a runner can assert the rejection -- that is the case working as intended and it is permanent; owned_gap is a reference that should resolve and does not, which is a protocol gap owned by a named spec report.
ratchet: owned_gap rows may only shrink: a new one is admissible only together with the spec report that owns it, and landing that report MUST remove the row rather than repoint the token. negative_token rows come and go with their fixture case, but a negative_token whose token becomes registered fails the gate: the case would then assert a rejection the registry contradicts. Any row whose token now resolves, or whose artifact no longer carries it, fails until the row is deleted.

references.reason: The case exists to show that a token satisfying the member's syntactic pattern is still refused because the registry does not list it. Registering this id would destroy the case.
An unknown operation version selector must yield unsupported_operation_version with zero route-cache writes and zero body parse attempts. The v9 suffix is the unknown version.
